name: Viktor
h1: Viktor ARR: ~$50M for the AI Coworker That Lives in Slack.
intro: Viktor is an AI coworker — a persistent agent that works alongside teams inside Slack, Teams and email, handling background research, drafting and follow-ups. Third-party estimates put its run rate around $50M, backed by a $75M Series A led by Accel at a $450M valuation. The reported numbers and their sources are below.

modelTitle: Charge for the Coworker, Not the Seat Counted in Tokens.
modelParagraphs: Viktor sells a persistent AI coworker that lives where work already happens: it joins Slack and Teams, keeps context across days, and takes recurring assignments — research, drafting, meeting prep, follow-ups — rather than answering one-off prompts. The pitch is an employee you delegate to, priced accordingly as a per-seat team subscription.

Because the product sits inside existing messaging surfaces, distribution rides the collaboration suite rather than a standalone app download — every teammate who watches the coworker deliver in-channel becomes a potential activated seat. That in-workflow visibility is what compresses the typical enterprise sales cycle for AI employees into a team-level credit-card purchase.
revenueMix: Per-seat pricing for the AI coworker across Slack and Teams workspaces.
Committed plans for departments standardizing on delegated background work.
In-channel visibility converts watchers into additional paid seats.

faqs.a: Around $50 million, estimated. Viktor has not disclosed revenue; the figure combines GetLatka's estimate with Leonis Capital's tracking showing roughly seven months from launch to $50M. Treat it as an estimate.

It is an AI coworker — a persistent agent inside Slack, Teams and email that takes recurring assignments like research, drafting and follow-ups, works in the background, and reports back in-channel. The framing is delegation to an employee, not prompting a chatbot.
A $75M Series A led by Accel in 2026 valued the company at $450M. Leonis Capital has also published on the company as part of its AI-employees thesis.
Per-seat team subscriptions, with annual contracts for departments. Pricing scales with the number of employees delegating work to the coworker rather than with tokens or API usage.

faqs.q: How Is Viktor Different from a Slack AI Assistant?
faqs.a: Slack-native assistants typically summarize threads on demand. Viktor keeps persistent context across days and owns multi-step background work end-to-end — closer to an additional teammate with a seat than a summarization feature.
